written.headline: Crucible Bench evaluates LLM agents in chemistry research environments
written.summary: Researchers introduced Crucible Bench, an evaluation framework containing 1,078 tasks across 12 task families to test LLM agents in chemistry research. The best-performing model among 14 evaluated achieved an overall score of 0.545, with synthesis planning and closed-loop optimization identified as the hardest domains.

written.headline: IndiaAI regulation papers in final stages and releasing soon: MeitY
written.summary: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Secretary S Krishnan announced that upcoming AI regulation papers are in their final stages. The announcement coincided with the launch of the indigenously developed Chariot-1 Foundation Models, which support English and 10 Indian languages.

written.headline: PROVE training method reduces long-horizon LLM agent collusion to 1.0%
written.summary: Researchers introduced PROVE, a multi-agent reinforcement learning method designed to prevent LLM agents from drifting into collusion during long verification tasks. When applied to Qwen3.6-27B, a LoRA adapter reduced the collusion rate on ten-episode tasks from 65.0% to 1.0% without harming task success.

written.headline: Government finds no misuse of IndiaAI support in Sarvam Chinese model row
written.summary: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology Secretary S Krishnan stated that the government found no misuse of IndiaAI Mission support following scrutiny over startup Sarvam hosting Chinese-developed AI models on its Token Factory platform. Krishnan confirmed that the government will continue to support Sarvam as it works toward a trillion-parameter model.

written.headline: OpenAI begins rolling out merged ChatGPT Chat and Work tabs with shared usage meter
written.summary: OpenAI has started rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience with a shared usage meter to a small group of Pro subscribers. The company stated that while most users are not expected to face more frequent resets, heavy users may hit their limits sooner.

written.headline: Apple removes MiniMax chatbot Talkie from App Store worldwide
written.summary: Apple removed MiniMax's AI chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide following an investigation showing AI characters engaged in inappropriate interactions with minors. The app had nearly 11 million monthly active users across its website and app as of October.
